next_state_election.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — 2026 Election Information

glance_notes.text: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Arizona's registration deadline is October 5 at 11:59 p.m., and early voting and the mailing of early ballots begin October 7.
glance_notes.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Calendar Dates

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register in Arizona, you must be a U.S. citizen, an Arizona resident and resident of the county listed on your registration, and at least 18 years old on or before the next regular General Election. Arizona also requires proof of residency. Registration is available through Arizona's official online system for eligible applicants and by paper form. Arizona has separate documentary-proof-of-citizenship rules that affect whether a registrant is eligible for a full state ballot or a federal-only ballot; voters who need to establish documentary proof of citizenship should follow the current Secretary of State and County Recorder instructions.
register.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Registration Requirements
register.internal_note: The current official registration-form instructions explain the full-ballot versus federal-only distinction. Because this area has active litigation and changing implementation, keep citizenship-proof details under frequent review.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Arizona's official Voter Information Portal to view your registration status and other voter information, including election districts, notices, ballot-by-mail status and voting history. If information is incorrect or you have moved, follow the state's registration-update process or contact your County Recorder.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, Arizona lists October 5, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. as the last day to register to vote. The Secretary of State's current procedures explain that online registration must be completed by 11:59 p.m. on the deadline; paper registrations delivered in person must be received by close of business, while mailed forms have separate timeliness rules based on postmark/date and receipt. UOCAVA voters have separate registration provisions.
deadlines.glance_value: October 5, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. for the November 3 General Election
deadlines.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Calendar Dates
deadlines.internal_note: Supplemental primary guidance: https://azsos.gov/elections/about-elections/elections-procedures/vr-procedures explains delivery-method timing and UOCAVA exceptions.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Arizona's official voter-information tools to find where to vote. The Secretary of State directs voters outside Maricopa and Pima counties to my.arizona.vote; its Election Day page provides separate links for Maricopa and Pima County voting locations. Because counties administer voting locations and locations can change, check the official state or county lookup for the current election.
polling_place.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Election Day Operations

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Arizona polling locations are open from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. In-person voters must present identification that satisfies Arizona's ID rules. A voter may use one qualifying item from the state's photo-ID list, two qualifying items from its non-photo list, or an allowed combination under the state's mix-and-match list. Arizona also uses provisional ballots as a fail-safe when eligibility or required documentation cannot be resolved at check-in; the ballot is counted only after the county determines that the voter is eligible and other applicable requirements are satisfied.
election_day.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Voting in Elections
election_day.internal_note: Election Day operations source also confirms 6 a.m.–7 p.m.: https://azsos.gov/elections/about-elections/elections-procedures/election-day-operations

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Arizona polling locations are open from 6:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Voters should use their county's official voting-location information for the correct location.
polling_hours.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Election Day Operations

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Arizona offers early voting before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins October 7. Valid identification is required before receiving a ballot at an in-person early-voting location. Voting locations and schedules are administered locally, so use the official Arizona voter portal or county election office for current locations and hours.
early_voting.glance_value: Begins October 7, 2026 for the November 3 General Election
early_voting.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Calendar Dates
early_voting.internal_note: Supplemental source for in-person ID requirement: https://azsos.gov/elections/voters/voting-elections

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Arizona allows eligible voters to request an early ballot by mail without giving an excuse. A ballot-by-mail request must be made no later than 11 days before Election Day; for November 3, 2026, that falls on October 23. Voted early ballots must be received by county election officials no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. They may be returned through authorized methods including mail, official drop boxes and voting locations. Arizona is an in-hand state: an Election Day postmark by itself is not enough if the ballot arrives after the deadline. Voters can track ballot status through the state's voter-information system.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Request by Oct. 23; ballot received by 7:00 p.m. Nov. 3, 2026
absentee_mail.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Early Voting Procedures
absentee_mail.internal_note: The 11-day request rule is also stated on current AZSOS election pages under A.R.S. §16-542(E). The June 29, 2026 AZSOS statement confirms Arizona remains an in-hand state.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Arizona requires identification for in-person voting, including Election Day, in-person early voting, emergency vote centers and special election boards. A voter may present one acceptable photo ID with the required name and address, two different acceptable non-photo documents, or an approved combination from the state's mix-and-match list. The official Secretary of State page maintains the current detailed lists, including government-issued IDs and qualifying documents such as utility bills, bank statements and official election mail. If identification or eligibility cannot be resolved at the voting location, provisional-ballot procedures may apply.
voter_id.glance_value: One qualifying photo ID, two qualifying non-photo documents, or an allowed combination
voter_id.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Voting in Elections

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Arizona requires accessible voting equipment at polling locations and vote centers. The Secretary of State says locations are selected with accessibility needs in mind and provides accessible voting devices, magnification tools, large-print materials and trained poll workers. Curbside voting is available for voters who cannot enter a voting location. A voter who needs help completing election materials or voting may receive assistance under the state's rules, including assistance at the polling place.
accessible_voting.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Voters / Accessible Voting

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Arizona provides a UOCAVA portal for qualifying uniformed-service members, eligible family members and overseas citizens to register and request an early ballot. Arizona's current procedures provide special registration timing for qualifying UOCAVA voters, and the state supports electronic processes for military and overseas voters. The 2026 General Election calendar lists September 19, 2026 as the UOCAVA deadline associated with that election. Voters using these procedures should follow the current UOCAVA portal instructions because federal and state rules differ from ordinary registration and ballot-by-mail procedures.
military_overseas.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Registering to Vote / UOCAVA
military_overseas.internal_note: Supplemental current sources: https://azsos.gov/elections/about-elections/elections-procedures/vr-procedures and the 2026 calendar. Arizona upgraded its UOCAVA portal in 2025.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: Arizona applies its ordinary voter-residency rules to students. A person's voting residence is the place the person treats as home and intends to return to when temporarily absent. Arizona election procedures specifically recognize college attendance as a reason a voter may be temporarily away from the residence where the voter is registered while intending to return. Students should register using the residence that satisfies Arizona's legal residency rules and should not assume that simply attending a school automatically establishes or ends an Arizona voting residence.
student_voting.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Voter Registration Procedures
student_voting.internal_note: The 2025 Elections Procedures Manual also expressly treats temporary absence for college attendance with intent to return as a valid residency circumstance.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Arizona counties mail sample ballots to voters who do not request a ballot by mail. For the 2026 General Election, state law as described by the Secretary of State requires Maricopa and Pima counties to mail sample ballots at least 11 days before the election, while the other counties must mail them at least 14 days before the election. Sample ballots include information about the ballot a voter will receive, acceptable in-person identification and where to vote. For election-specific ballot content, use the official 2026 election page and your county election authority.
sample_ballot.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — 2026 Election Information
sample_ballot.internal_note: The 2026 page attributes the county-specific mailing timing to A.R.S. §16-461(D), as amended by Laws 2026, Chapter 34. General pre-election procedures: https://azsos.gov/elections/about-elections/elections-procedures/pre-election-procedures

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Arizona Secretary of State, Elections Division: 1700 W. Washington St., Floor 7, Phoenix, AZ 85007-2808. Elections Services phone: 602-542-8683. Toll-free in Arizona: 1-877-THE-VOTE. The Secretary of State also provides an Elections contact form and a directory of County Recorders and county election departments.
contact.source_name: Arizona Secretary of State — Contact Us

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: The Arizona Secretary of State elections website is the state's central source for registration requirements, election calendars, voting rules, election procedures and statewide election information. The Arizona Voter Information Portal provides personal voter information such as registration status, election districts, notices, ballot-by-mail status and voting history. Arizona's 15 County Recorders and county election departments are the primary local sources for county-administered registration, ballot-by-mail and voting-location information.
official_resources.internal_note: County directory: https://azsos.gov/elections/about-elections/county-election-contact-info ; voter portal is linked from https://azsos.gov/elections/voters
